clue.text: I apologise for breaking pomander

indicators.note: breaking the word pomander apart lets its letters be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says sorry after smashing a scented pomander ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' signals an anagram of POMANDER; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite spoken phrases of contrition, said after a small social slip.

clue.text: Stop going to and fro

indicators.note: going to and fro says the letters read the same in either direction, forwards and back

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop pacing back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to and fro' tells you the answer is a palindrome: it reads identically backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt a vehicle or a movement is to draw it to a standstill, a common phrasal verb.

clue.text: Cheap paper carrier containing jumble

parts.note: a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper
a carrier bag holds shopping

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper bag full of jumble-sale goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' is only a link here; the two pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscellaneous, disorderly collection of things is a hotchpotch or medley.

clue.text: Barbecue party is better

definitions.meaning: read as ..., an open-air social event

explanation.surface: A barbecue gathering turns out to be an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as OUT (outdoors) plus DO (a party); the second is the ordinary verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is an open-air gathering, and the verb means to exceed a rival in performance.

clue.text: Canadian lawman's moment to loose the bonds

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, as in 'half a mo'
to free knots or ties is to undo them

explanation.surface: A Canadian police officer has a brief chance to free a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'lawman' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police are known by this informal name.

clue.text: A bishop just must be cheerful

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
just means fair or correct

explanation.surface: A clergyman is told he simply has to look happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'simply' but means RIGHT (fair).
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny, lively, optimistic manner is a synonym for cheerful.

clue.text: Checked that the ironing had been done again

definitions.text: that the ironing had been done again
definitions.meaning: read as ..., pressed once more with an iron

explanation.surface: Someone verified that the clothes were ironed a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings held in check are kept down, and clothes ironed anew are pressed a second time.

clue.text: Suffer from cephalalgia, but make progress nonetheless

definitions.meaning: cephalalgia is the medical word for headache; to acquire a sore head
to advance or succeed in life

explanation.surface: Someone with a headache still manages to advance.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as GET A HEAD, slang for developing a headache, especially a hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop a sore head, and to move forward in a career, share the same letters.

clue.text: Drunken gents drowned in wine cask of metal

indicators.note: the gents end up in the cask, the cask's letters coming first here

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

indicators.note: drunken men stagger about, so the letters of gents are jumbled

explanation.surface: Inebriated men drowned in a barrel of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' signals the anagram of the men, and 'drowned in' puts them into the cask, here after its letters; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy grey element, used for lamp filaments, is one example of this class of material.

clue.text: Gets sparkling, low-alcohol drink

parts.note: light beers are low in alcohol
to sup is to drink in sips

explanation.surface: Someone becomes lively after a weak drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A face that brightens with joy illuminates, the phrasal verb for becoming radiant.

clue.text: The star is in the limelight -and quite right!

definitions.text: The star is in the limelight
definitions.meaning: the spotlight is switched on the performer

explanation.surface: An actor centre stage is praised as exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotlight shining on a performer, and an accurate guess, share the same phrase.

clue.text: He occasions a furious comeback

indicators.note: a comeback reverses direction, so the word for furious is read backwards

parts.note: mad means angry

explanation.surface: A man provokes an angry retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' turns the word for furious round behind the A; 'occasions' is a link. 'He' is the first man in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's first man is the archetypal male person, so a pronoun for a man fits.

clue.text: Dan pouted in distress when rejected

indicators.note: distress suggests things in disorder, so the letters of Dan pouted are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dan sulked unhappily on being turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' signals an anagram of DAN POUTED; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A road not taken over by the council, or a child not taken into a family, is spurned or not accepted.

clue.text: In any case, those are the prevailing attitudes

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words any case, those

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, those are the dominant views.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in 'casE THOSe'; 'In any case' looks like a set phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit or beliefs of a community or era make up its outlook.

clue.text: Confront a fellow-expert

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to a colleague who is equally skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a challenge head-on is to stand up to it.

clue.text: Pat and Ernest have split up now

indicators.note: splitting up breaks Pat and Ernest apart so their letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple named Pat and Ernest have separated recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening at this moment is happening currently.

clue.text: A learned man is wise to get his pound of flesh

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
the 's contraction of is
sage means wise

explanation.surface: A scholar insists on his due, like Shylock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound of flesh' is Shylock's bond in The Merchant of Venice, but here means kneading the body; 'to get his' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading and pummelling muscles is a pounding of the body's soft tissue.

clue.text: Family member consumes all the vegetables

definitions.note: plural in the clue for a single onion-like vegetable

indicators.note: consuming takes something inside, so all goes into the family member

parts.note: a scion is a descendant of a family

explanation.surface: A relative eats all the greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' means the family member swallows the word all; 'the' is a link and the plural 'vegetables' is loose for a single one.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring onion is a green plant eaten as food.

clue.text: Daughter is relaxed, but full of complaint

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
eased means loosened or relaxed

explanation.surface: A girl is calm but keeps grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an illness, not a grumble; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment, so being riddled with one is being sick.

clue.text: Conductress has to trim the pastry

parts.note: to clip is to cut or trim
a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A woman in charge has to cut the pastry crust.
explanation.walkthrough: A CLIPPIE was a female bus conductor in Britain, who clipped tickets; 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for a woman who punched tickets on a bus.

clue.text: Wickedness quick to be shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the letters run upwards, backwards

parts.note: quick is an old word for alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing is soon exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' means living here, not fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral badness or sin is a close synonym.

clue.text: Support a Verdi opera

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Backing for a production by the Italian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Egyptian tragedy of 1871 is named after its Ethiopian princess heroine.

clue.text: Man needs a woman without sex appeal

indicators.note: without is old usage for outside, so the woman goes around the sex appeal

parts.note: a dame is a woman
IT is crossword shorthand for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A man wants a woman lacking allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking; 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant of the first man in Genesis is a human being.

clue.text: Resist giving operation to model

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to let a model have surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand against or fight something is to contest it.

clue.text: Old bangers many costs

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number
rates are charges or prices

explanation.surface: Old sausages cost a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: A BANGER is British slang for both a sausage and a decrepit old car.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickety old cars are informally called by this name for packing boxes.

clue.text: Subject from a Belgian province

definitions.meaning: a province and city in eastern Belgium

explanation.surface: A citizen hails from somewhere in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal vassal owed allegiance, and the Walloon city of that name gives its province its title.

clue.text: Pitmen are wild-really wild

indicators.note: wild suggests letters running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: Miners are furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'wild' is the anagram signal; 'really wild' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a rage or very angry is a state of fury.

clue.text: Happening to find an outlet after June's end

indicators.note: after places the outlet behind June's last letter
the last letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the last letter of June is E
a vent is an opening for release

explanation.surface: Something occurs once June is over, giving release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An occurrence or incident is something that takes place.

clue.text: Supplied — with a summons?

explanation.surface: Someone was served papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IS SUED: one who is summoned is being sued.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment given out is distributed, and someone served with a writ is being prosecuted.

clue.text: Local owner employing lot of colliers

definitions.meaning: the landlord of a pub, a local
read as ..., a pit hosting a crowd of miners

explanation.surface: A pub landlord runs a pit full of miners.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is British slang for a neighbourhood pub; MINE HOST is the old jocular term for its landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Old jocular term for a publican or innkeeper, and a colliery with a host of workers.

clue.text: It reveals the bare essentials

parts.note: the state of being unclothed literally displays bare essential body parts

explanation.surface: Something summarises the key points.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclothed exposes the body uncovered, punning on bare essentials as basics.

clue.text: Agitated appeal to be more energetic

definitions.meaning: read as ..., an urging to idle less

explanation.surface: An anxious person is told to get moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidgety and uneasy means unsettled, and urging someone to idle less tells them to slack less.
